Paper_Title: Eyeriss: An Energy-Efficient Accelerator for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
PE_Organization: Fixed 12x14 PE array; static spatial mapping
Metrics_Reported: Measured Silicon Power (278 mW), Energy/MAC (pJ), Frame Rate
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Exploits ReLU activation zeros to gate datapath switching and memory reads
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: Eyeriss has fixed 168 PEs and custom Row-Stationary NoC; Neural_Acc provides dynamic 16/32/64 PE allocation with hardware policy controller
Comparison_Limitations: Eyeriss has physical 65nm silicon measurements; Neural_Acc evaluated via cycle-accurate RTL simulation

Paper_Title: Cnvlutin: Ineffectual-Neuron-Free Deep Neural Network Computing
Architecture: Decoupled Lane SIMD Compute Engine with Offset FIFOs
PE_Organization: Fixed 16-lane processing clusters with decoupled queues
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Skips zero-activation multiplications and suppresses associated weight fetches
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: Cnvlutin uses asynchronous FIFO buffers to compress cycles and achieve latency speedup; Neural_Acc maintains synchronous channel-chunk stepping (0.00% speedup)
Comparison_Limitations: Cnvlutin uses simulation-level energy models; does not support dynamic PE count resizing

Paper_Title: SCNN: An Accelerator for Compressed-sparse Convolutional Neural Networks
Architecture: Planar PE Array with Cartesian Product Crossbar & Multiplier Grids
Sparsity_Type: Dual Sparsity (Weights and Activations in Compressed Coordinate Format)
PE_Organization: 4x4 PE array with internal multiplier arrays
Evaluation_Platform: Custom cycle-level simulator + Synopsys 16nm TSMC Cell Library
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Exploits activation zeros in convolutional layers to reduce computation
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: SCNN processes both sparse weights and activations in compressed coordinate format using Cartesian crossbars; Neural_Acc focuses on dense weights with zero-activation suppression
Comparison_Limitations: SCNN incurs high crossbar and scratchpad bank conflict overheads; evaluated at 16nm standard cells

Paper_Title: Cambricon-X: An accelerator for sparse neural networks
Architecture: Asynchronous Indexing Processing Engine with Indexing Matching Logic
PE_Organization: 16 PEs with 16 multipliers each (256 multipliers total)
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Eliminates unneeded MAC operations and memory access to reduce energy
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: Cambricon-X skips zero weights via index matching; Neural_Acc skips zero activations and supports dynamic 16/32/64 PE allocation
Comparison_Limitations: Different sparsity target (weight vs activation); Cambricon-X lacks hardware latency budget arbitration

Paper_Title: NullHop: A Flexible Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator Based on Sparse Representations of Feature Maps
Publication: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
Architecture: Custom Sparsity Exploitation Core with Compression Indexes
Metrics_Reported: Effective Compute Throughput (MAC/s), FPGA Resource Utilization, Speedup
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Exploits ReLU activation sparsity; handles multi-channel 3x3 convolution
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: NullHop compresses activations into non-zero streams with pointer tables to gain latency speedup; Neural_Acc operates synchronously without pointer tables and provides dynamic PE partitioning
Comparison_Limitations: NullHop requires pointer table storage overhead; does not support dynamic PE resizing

Paper_Title: Eyeriss v2: A Flexible Accelerator for Emerging Deep Neural Networks on Mobile Devices
Publication: IEEE Journal on Emerging and Selected Topics in Circuits and Systems (JETCAS)
Architecture: Hierarchical Mesh NoC with Scalable Processing Clusters
Sparsity_Type: Sparse Weights and Sparse Activations (CSC Format)
PE_Organization: Hierarchical Array (8 Clusters x 24 PEs = 192 PEs)
Resource_Adaptation: Configurable (Spatial mapping reconfigures for Depthwise/Sparse layers)
Evaluation_Platform: Simulated 65nm CMOS Core + CACTI Memory Models
Metrics_Reported: Throughput (FPS), Energy Efficiency (uJ/inf) across MobileNet and AlexNet
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Configurable processing clusters and activation/weight zero-skipping
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: Eyeriss v2 relies on flexible On-Chip Network (NoC) routing for mapping; Neural_Acc uses multi-pass channel tiling and explicit latency-budget policy arbitration in hardware
Comparison_Limitations: Eyeriss v2 uses complex router routers; Neural_Acc uses dedicated multibank SRAM crossbar

Paper_Title: SparTen: A Sparse Tensor Accelerator for Convolutional Neural Networks
Architecture: Dual-Sparsity Accelerator with Greedy Prefix-Sum Coordination
Sparsity_Type: Dual Sparsity (Weight and Activation Zero Skipping)
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Exploits activation sparsity in CNNs to prevent unproductive MAC operations
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: SparTen uses greedy coordination logic to align sparse weights and activations for speedup; Neural_Acc prioritizes deterministic latency and adapts PE hardware allocation
Comparison_Limitations: SparTen has complex scheduling overheads; does not adapt PE count dynamically

Paper_Title: nZESPA: A Near-3D-Memory Zero Skipping Parallel Accelerator for CNNs
Publication: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems (TCAD)
Architecture: Near-Memory Processing Vaults with Zero-Skipping Logic
PE_Organization: Distributed PEs integrated near Hybrid Memory Cube (HMC) vaults
Metrics_Reported: Speedup (3.2x), Memory Bandwidth Reduction, Energy Savings
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Suppresses memory accesses and arithmetic operations associated with zero activations
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: nZESPA relies on 3D-stacked memory (HMC) near-memory vault logic; Neural_Acc uses conventional multi-bank 2D SRAM and dynamic PE reconfiguration
Comparison_Limitations: nZESPA relies on high-bandwidth 3D memory technology that is costly for edge IoT

Paper_Title: DianNao: A Small-Footprint High-Throughput Accelerator for Ubiquitous Machine-Learning
Architecture: Neural Processing Unit with NFU (Neural Functional Unit) Pipeline
PE_Organization: Fixed 64-multiplier NFU (16x16 input multipliers, adder trees)
Metrics_Reported: Throughput (452 GMAC/s), Power (485 mW), Area (3.02 mm2)
Similarities_To_Neural_Acc: Provides dedicated on-chip SRAM buffer hierarchy (NBin, SB, NBout) for CNN tiling
Differences_From_Neural_Acc: DianNao is completely dense (processes all zeros) and lacks adaptive PE allocation; Neural_Acc adds activation zero-gating and dynamic 16/32/64 PE allocation
Comparison_Limitations: Foundational dense baseline; lacks sparsity and dynamic resource reconfigurability

Paper_Title: Neural_Acc: Activation-Sparse CNN Accelerator with Adaptive PE Allocation and Multi-Pass Memory Trade-Off Analysis
Architecture: Reconfigurable Multi-Bank Spatial Array (16, 32, 64 PEs) with Autonomous Hardware Sequencer
PE_Organization: Configurable 16-, 32-, and 64-PE partitions with multi-pass channel tiling
Resource_Adaptation: Dynamic Hardware Policy Controller (Policy A: Min Resource, Policy B: Max Performance)
Evaluation_Platform: Cycle-accurate RTL (SystemVerilog) + Master Regression Suite + Python Golden Reference
Metrics_Reported: Exact Cycle Counts, Compute Cycles (-48% to -85%), Weight SRAM Reads (-48% to -85%), Activation SRAM Reads (+100% to +300%), Numerical MAE (0.0)
Comparison_Limitations: Evaluated at cycle-accurate RTL level across representative 4x4 spatial patches of real CNN layers; physical ASIC power characterization remains future work
